title: Seafood & Smoke Board
seo_title: Seafood Charcuterie Board for 8–12: Smoked Salmon & Shrimp
description: A seafood charcuterie board for 8–12: smoked salmon, smoked trout, shrimp cocktail, cream cheese, Boursin, capers, dill, cucumber and everything bagel chips.
hook: Coastal flavors with smoked salmon at the center: a seafood board that feels elegant and a little unexpected.
why: Smoked salmon is the anchor: rich, salty and deep pink in long folds across the middle. Flaked smoked trout has a lighter smoke and sits between the salmon and the cream cheese, so the flavors step down gently. Sweet, mild shrimp gives everyone a break from the smoke.
Capers, red onion, lemon and dill are what make smoked fish taste clean, and cream cheese and Boursin carry them. Keep the seafood cold until the last minute and serve on a chilled platter.

timeline.what: Take the cream cheese out to soften; keep the seafood cold.
Shape the cream cheese; slice the cucumber.
Place the cheeses; set out the capers and onion.
Lay the salmon, trout and shrimp; add lemon and dill.

faq.q: What goes on a seafood charcuterie board?
faq.a: Smoked salmon, smoked trout, cooked shrimp, cream cheese, herbed cheese, capers, red onion, cucumber, lemon, dill, sauces and sturdy crackers.

faq.q: How long can seafood sit out?
faq.a: No more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. Set it on a chilled platter and refill from the fridge.

faq.q: Is smoked salmon safe during pregnancy?
faq.a: Refrigerated cold-smoked salmon is on the CDC's list to avoid during pregnancy unless it's cooked. Shrimp cocktail (cooked) is fine if it's kept cold.
